lines.trans: Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
He took a second bite! Salma, he did not make the brass-polish face!
Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.
Aha! Caught you asking for seconds, Mr Tough Judge!
Eat all you want, Mazen, and write down four full cakes for Saturday!
Keep baking like this, Salma, and half of Amman will line up outside our gate.

meanings.note: The word 'هيو' (هيو) means 'هيو'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هيو القاضي مازن أخد الشوكة الأولى—ولا حدا يحكي ولا كلمة!
examples.trans: Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
This is هيو.

meanings.note: The word 'القاضي' (القاضي) means 'القاضي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهادا القاضي مازن لابس نظارات القراءة تبعونه، ومبين جدي كتير الصراحة.
examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is القاضي.

meanings.note: The word 'مازن' (مازن) means 'مازن'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرة واحدة فوق يا مازن، وسلكك اللطيف رن مرتين متل العادة.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell once upstairs, Mazen, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.
This is مازن.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: The word 'الشوكة' (الشوكة) means 'الشوكة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هيو القاضي مازن أخد الشوكة الأولى—ولا حدا يحكي ولا كلمة!
examples.trans: Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
This is الشوكة.

meanings.note: The word 'الأولى—ولا' (الأولى—ولا) means 'الأولى—ولا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هيو القاضي مازن أخد الشوكة الأولى—ولا حدا يحكي ولا كلمة!
examples.trans: Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
This is الأولى—ولا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'someone / anyone'; with ما في (ما في حدا) it means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The word 'يحكي' (يحكي) means 'يحكي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هيو القاضي مازن أخد الشوكة الأولى—ولا حدا يحكي ولا كلمة!
examples.trans: Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
This is يحكي.

meanings.note: With two pronunciations in context: walla ('or' in choice questions: عالشارع ولا عالساحة؟) and wala ('not even / nor': ولا خدش 'not a single scratch', ولا يهمك 'do not worry at all').

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كلمات.

examples.trans: She did not say a single word to anyone.
The word thank you warms the heart.

meanings.note: The word 'لاحظوا' (لاحظوا) means 'لاحظوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لاحظوا كيف الشوكة بتدخل دغري من غير شاكوش أو نظارات واقية.
examples.trans: Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
This is لاحظوا.

meanings.note: Question word 'how?'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: The word 'بتدخل' (بتدخل) means 'بتدخل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لاحظوا كيف الشوكة بتدخل دغري من غير شاكوش أو نظارات واقية.
examples.trans: Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
This is بتدخل.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine word (from Turkish doğru) meaning 'straight ahead' in directions.

examples.trans: Turn left and walk straight to the bridge.
Walk straight to the end of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: The word 'شاكوش' (شاكوش) means 'شاكوش'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لاحظوا كيف الشوكة بتدخل دغري من غير شاكوش أو نظارات واقية.
examples.trans: Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
This is شاكوش.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: The word 'نظارات' (نظارات) means 'نظارات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهادا القاضي مازن لابس نظارات القراءة تبعونه، ومبين جدي كتير الصراحة.
examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is نظارات.

meanings.note: The word 'واقية' (واقية) means 'واقية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لاحظوا كيف الشوكة بتدخل دغري من غير شاكوش أو نظارات واقية.
examples.trans: Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
This is واقية.

meanings.note: The word 'استنوا' (استنوا) means 'استنوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا... خلوا الزلمة يمضغ منيح قبل ما تبلشوا تحتفلوا إنتو التنتين.
examples.trans: Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
This is استنوا.

meanings.note: The word 'الزلمة' (الزلمة) means 'الزلمة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا... خلوا الزلمة يمضغ منيح قبل ما تبلشوا تحتفلوا إنتو التنتين.
examples.trans: Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
This is الزلمة.

meanings.note: The word 'يمضغ' (يمضغ) means 'يمضغ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يمضغ ببطء كتير... أوف لا، حواجبه عم يقربوا من بعض.
examples.trans: He is chewing very slowly... oh no, his eyebrows are moving closer together.
This is يمضغ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: The word 'تبلشوا' (تبلشوا) means 'تبلشوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا... خلوا الزلمة يمضغ منيح قبل ما تبلشوا تحتفلوا إنتو التنتين.
examples.trans: Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
This is تبلشوا.

meanings.note: The word 'تحتفلوا' (تحتفلوا) means 'تحتفلوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا... خلوا الزلمة يمضغ منيح قبل ما تبلشوا تحتفلوا إنتو التنتين.
examples.trans: Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
This is تحتفلوا.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: The word 'التنتين' (التنتين) means 'التنتين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا... خلوا الزلمة يمضغ منيح قبل ما تبلشوا تحتفلوا إنتو التنتين.
examples.trans: Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
This is التنتين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لقم.

examples.trans: Taste just one bite of the cake!
We had a quick bite before work.

meanings.note: The word 'تانية' (تانية) means 'تانية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أخد لقمة تانية! يا سلمى، ما عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس!
examples.trans: He took a second bite! Salma, he did not make the brass-polish face!
This is تانية.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: The word 'سلمى' (سلمى) means 'سلمى'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خلينا ناخده طوالي لـ سلمى بغرفة تسعة قبل ما حدا يتنفس بقوة!
examples.trans: Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!
This is سلمى.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: The word 'كشرة' (كشرة) means 'كشرة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنتي شجاعة يا سلمى. إذا عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس، رح نضطر نعيد كل شي من أول وجديد!
examples.trans: You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!
This is كشرة.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: The word 'وهلق' (وهلق) means 'وهلق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is وهلق.

meanings.note: The word 'احكيلنا' (احكيلنا) means 'احكيلنا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is احكيلنا.

meanings.note: The word 'بصراحة—هل' (بصراحة—هل) means 'بصراحة—هل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is بصراحة—هل.

meanings.note: The word 'هالكيكة' (هالكيكة) means 'هالكيكة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is هالكيكة.

meanings.note: The word 'بتستاهل' (بتستاهل) means 'بتستاهل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is بتستاهل.

meanings.note: The word 'تنحط' (تنحط) means 'تنحط'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is تنحط.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: The word 'الذكرى' (الذكرى) means 'الذكرى'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is الذكرى.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!

meanings.note: Saturday (يوم السبت or simply السبت), start of the Jordanian working/market weekend.

examples.text: كل سبت الصبح بنمشي عسوق الحارة.
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning we walk to the neighbourhood market.

examples.text: الخبز الطازة بيجهز يوم السبت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Fresh bread is ready on Saturday at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: The word 'ناوليني' (ناوليني) means 'ناوليني'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ناوليني دفتر الورق تبعي وقلم النجار الرصاص من جنب الإبريق يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
This is ناوليني.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: The word 'وقلم' (وقلم) means 'وقلم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ناوليني دفتر الورق تبعي وقلم النجار الرصاص من جنب الإبريق يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
This is وقلم.

meanings.note: The word 'النجار' (النجار) means 'النجار'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ناوليني دفتر الورق تبعي وقلم النجار الرصاص من جنب الإبريق يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
This is النجار.

meanings.note: The word 'الرصاص' (الرصاص) means 'الرصاص'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ناوليني دفتر الورق تبعي وقلم النجار الرصاص من جنب الإبريق يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
This is الرصاص.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'next to, beside'.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: The word 'الإبريق' (الإبريق) means 'الإبريق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ناوليني دفتر الورق تبعي وقلم النجار الرصاص من جنب الإبريق يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
This is الإبريق.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: The word 'يكتب' (يكتب) means 'يكتب'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يكتب بحروف كبيرة... عشرة من عشرة، لا تغيروا ولا إشي!
examples.trans: He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
This is يكتب.

meanings.note: The word 'بحروف' (بحروف) means 'بحروف'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يكتب بحروف كبيرة... عشرة من عشرة، لا تغيروا ولا إشي!
examples.trans: He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
This is بحروف.

meanings.note: The word 'كبيرة' (كبيرة) means 'كبيرة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لأنه في قطرة مطر كبيرة خبطت الحبر الأزرق بالزبط عالطبقة الدافية السرية!
examples.trans: Because one big raindrop hit the blue ink right on the secret warm glaze!
This is كبيرة.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: The word 'تغيروا' (تغيروا) means 'تغيروا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يكتب بحروف كبيرة... عشرة من عشرة، لا تغيروا ولا إشي!
examples.trans: He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
This is تغيروا.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: The word 'يس' (يس) means 'يس'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يس! عشرة من عشرة بقلم مازن بتسوى تلات ميداليات ذهبية!
examples.trans: YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
This is يس.

meanings.note: The word 'بتسوى' (بتسوى) means 'بتسوى'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يس! عشرة من عشرة بقلم مازن بتسوى تلات ميداليات ذهبية!
examples.trans: YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
This is بتسوى.

meanings.note: The word 'ميداليات' (ميداليات) means 'ميداليات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يس! عشرة من عشرة بقلم مازن بتسوى تلات ميداليات ذهبية!
examples.trans: YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
This is ميداليات.

meanings.note: The word 'ذهبية' (ذهبية) means 'ذهبية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يس! عشرة من عشرة بقلم مازن بتسوى تلات ميداليات ذهبية!
examples.trans: YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
This is ذهبية.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: The word 'السلامة' (السلامة) means 'السلامة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بس عشان السلامة الهيكلية، لازم أختبر كمان شقفة صغيرة من الزاوية.
examples.trans: Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.
This is السلامة.

meanings.note: The word 'الهيكلية' (الهيكلية) means 'الهيكلية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.
This is الهيكلية.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Expresses equal amount or degree: قدنا مرتين ('twice as much as us'), قد ما بقدر ('as much as I can').

examples.trans: Tariq is twice as curious as we are!

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!
